title: What the Foot Can Push With: The Leg Jacobian, the Joint Torques That Hold a Body Up, and Why a Bent Knee Costs More Than a Straight One

questions.question: What connects the foot's force to the joints' torques?
options: The inverse kinematics, solved once for each force
The motor constant and the gear ratio
The Jacobian's transpose, by virtual work
The leg's mass matrix
questions.explanation: The work done at the foot equals the work done at the joints, which makes the torques the transpose of the Jacobian times the force. No dynamics are needed for a leg that is standing.

questions.question: The knee's torque for the crouch was:
options: 0.00 N m, since the foot is under the hip
questions.explanation: With the foot 0.20 m below the hip the knee gave 5.43 N m; at 0.30 m it was 4.33, and nearly straight at 0.40 m only 1.88. The zero belongs to the hip's pitch joint.

questions.question: Why does a straight leg need less torque?
options: The foot carries less of the body's weight when the leg is long
The thigh and shank share the load equally when in line
The motor's constant is larger near full stretch
The force goes along the bones, so the shank's lean from the vertical is small
questions.explanation: The knee's torque is the load times the horizontal distance from the knee to the line of the force. Straighten the leg and that distance shrinks to nothing.

questions.question: The knee rate for 0.5 m/s at 0.40 m was:
options: 15.5 rad/s
3.4 rad/s
0.5 rad/s, the same as the foot
5.43 rad/s
questions.explanation: The same foot speed needed 3.4 rad/s at 0.30 m and 15.5 rad/s at 0.40 m. The closer to straight, the more the knee has to turn for each millimetre.

questions.question: What does the inverse of the transpose give?
options: The joint rates for a foot velocity
The force at the foot from the torques measured at the joints
The torques that hold a force at the foot
The foot's place from the joint angles
questions.explanation: The transpose turns a foot force into torques, so its inverse turns measured torques back into the force. It fails, and says so, where the leg is singular.

questions.question: What is not in this model?
options: The share of the weight on each foot
Friction, the legs' own weight, and acceleration
The difference between a left and a right leg
The lever of the weight about the knee
questions.explanation: The torques are those of a leg at rest holding a load. The leg's own mass, friction in the gears and the torque to accelerate are all left out.
